Setting $\deriv{\sigma^2}\ell = 0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= -\frac{n}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
 + \frac{1}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(score for $\sigma^2$)}\\
\frac{n}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-1}
&= \frac{1}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(add $\tfrac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}$)}\\
\sigma^2 &= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(multiply by $2(\sigma^2)^2/n$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the maximizer $\mu = \bar x$,
which does not depend on $\sigma^2$
(a technique called profiling), gives:

$$\hat{\sigma}^2_{\text{ML}} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar x)^2$$

The profile log-likelihood
$\ell(\bar x, \sigma^2) = -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2} - \frac{n\hat\sigma^2_{\text{ML}}}{2\sigma^2}$
increases for $\sigma^2 < \hat\sigma^2_{\text{ML}}$
and decreases for $\sigma^2 > \hat\sigma^2_{\text{ML}}$,
because its derivative, $\frac{n}{2}\paren{\sigma^2}^{-2}\paren{\hat\sigma^2_{\text{ML}} - \sigma^2}$,
has the sign of $\hat\sigma^2_{\text{ML}} - \sigma^2$.
So $(\bar x, \hat\sigma^2_{\text{ML}})$ is the global maximizer,
provided the $x_i$ are not all equal.

::: notes
Differentiating with respect to $\sigma^2$ as a single variable,
rather than with respect to $\sigma$, keeps the algebra short.
Replacing $\sigma^2$ with the precision $\tau \eqdef 1/\sigma^2$
and differentiating with respect to $\tau$
can be shorter still,
because $\tau$ enters the log-likelihood as
$\frac{n}{2}\log\tau - \frac{\tau}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2$.
By the invariance of maximum likelihood estimates,
$\hat\tau_{\text{ML}} = 1/\hat\sigma^2_{\text{ML}}$.
:::

::: notes
This MLE divides by $n$,
so it is a biased estimator of $\sigma^2$
([bias of the divide-by-$n$ estimator](estimation.qmd#exm-biased-variance-mle)).
:::
